Okay, you were warned.

So let me start by saying that I think the whole movie takes place in Ophelia's head in the moments before she dies. It's all a dream. Reality mixes with fantasy as she hallucinates in her final moments while the last few days of her life flash before her eyes. This is shown to us in the opening of the film where she lays dying. It's our first strong piece of evidence about what's really happening.

Since she is hallucinating the events of the film, she is an unreliable narrator. Even things which are supposed to have taken place in reality, separate or partially intertwined from the fantasy fairy tale world, may not have actually happened as we see them, or may not have happened at all. What we do know is that she is still very childish, doesn't understand the grown up world, and she is very much into fairy tales. She's also been surrounded by war and her life is affected by it right up until the moment she is shot and killed.

So what really happened? Hard to say. All we know is what Ophelia thinks happened as she lays dying, half alive, and half into a hallucinatory dream world of near death, her traumatized brain still trying to make coherent sense of all the horrible death and suffering she has seen, and she does this through the lens of a child obsessed with fairy tales, trying to cope with all of it, including her own death. She constructs a narrative that separates her from these traumatic events by placing herself elsewhere off on her quests while they are happening. It's also a narrative that allows her to die with a contented smile, believing that she is now an immortal princess, while her brother is rescued from the evil villain who is served justice by receiving deadly violence at the hands of those he inflicted it on.

It's been a slow night. It's been four hours and I've only had two calls and one successful repo. So my coworker and I are just fucking around at the lot, racing each other up and down the street and teasing each other. We finally get a call around 1am for a guy who's car wouldn't start so he could leave his job. I won the rock, paper, scissors to take it and headed out to pick the guy up.

I arrived at the pizza shop the car was at and was met by a human-sized young man. After talking to him for a few minutes, and failing to jump start the car, I offered to drive him to a dealership or auto center to have his starter and ignition system checked. He declined, saying his dad could fix it and his mother was already headed to pick him up.

I loaded up his car and we waited and made small talk while waiting for his mother. After about 10 minutes, another car pulls in and, after minutes of maneuvering and struggling, a semi truck emerged from the small sedan. If that Camry could talk, I wouldn't want to hear it's stories. They wanted it towed to an unfamiliar area, close to the next county over, so I said I'd just follow them home. And off we go.

The total distance was a little under 30 miles. Should have been a quick, easy trip to their house and a quick drop off. Nope. After about 10 miles, I see the car get in the turning lane and follow them into a Wawa parking lot.Thinking they were going to get gas, I pulled up in the big space where the gas tankers usually stop to fill up the tanks and wait. They don't pull up to a pump. They pull up right in front of the door and the struggle to escape the small car was repeated. Maybe she had to pee and it couldn't wait? No. Through the front windows, I saw her head straight to the area where they make your food order and start placing one on the computer. I get out the truck and head over to the son, who was still sitting in the car.

"What is she doing?"

"She said she needed food. I told her to wait, but she said her sugars were dropping." The tone in his voice suggested he knew she was full of shit, and was embarrassed. So I headed inside to talk to her. The only other patrons where a a team of fat truckers, a group of hams(dad and spawn) that I'm guessing where tourists passing through, and a random guy (the only other human here) who I guess was a night worker.

"Hey, why are we stopping?" I asked.

"I need some food. My sugars are low." She replied, as she clicked though her order on the screen. "If you want a snack, grab some. You need to eat girl."

"Alright." I replied. So I followed over to the drink machine and copied her drink. We both grabbed the largest cup (44oz) and filled it up with Diet Coke. She headed over to the chip aisle and I headed over to the snack cakes, where the fat truckers where with their hands full of doughnuts and danishes, and started picking up and reading the nutrition labels out loud.

"Wow, there so many calories in a doughnut! Oooh, an iced honeybun? Damn it's so many calories. That's too many for today." I saw them put back all but one each as I walked away.

My next stop was the aisle with candy where the ham family was deciding what to get. I saw each Junior Ham(maybe 10 and 13 years old?) grab a king size candy bar and start begging their dad for them, as he started picking out his own candy. I grabbed a king size Hershey bar.

"Whoa, almost 400 calories in one bar? That's more than I eat in a meal!" I looked in the dad's direction, pretending to think out loud "Too many calories. Maybe I'll just get some fruit instead. Don't want to get fat." And I put the bar back and walked over to check out the fruit selection. I saw the dad say something to the kids and then they put the candy back and came over and grabbed some apple slices with yogurt dip instead. I selected their personal tray of pita chips and hummus dip (comes with about 8 chips and 2oz of hummus) and two bananas and met up with Ham Mom as she was collecting her sandwich.

"Is that all your getting?" She asked, with a snobby tone.

"Yes. I'm going to share with the other guy working tonight since I'm watching my figure and I'm sure he's hungry by now. And this soda will be a nice treat for us too." I replied.

"Oh." she said, looking at her sandwich box, two bags of chips, beef jerky stick, and granola bar.

She paid for our food, leaving the beef jerky and a bag of chips behind. Then we were back on our way.

The rest of the trip was uneventful, except for her hands being covered in whatever sauce was on her sub (mayo and ranch mixed together?) when she snatched the receipt out of my hand after the son finished paying me and signing it.

And yep, we split the snack tray, soda, and each had a banana for a nice 3am dinner.
